newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Centaur boosts gold resources in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Centaur boosts gold resources in quarter.

text.p: Centaur Mining and Exploration Ltd said on Friday it had increased its overall mineral resource estimate to 7.2 million ounces of gold, comprising 85.5 million tonnes at 2.6 grammes per tonne (g/t) gold.
Centaur said this represented an increase of 1.6 million ounces on the quarter and 5.9 million ounces for the past year.

Proved and probable gold reserves had now been estimated at 1.1 million ounces, comprising 8.4 million at 2.9 g/t gold for 793,000 ounces at Mt Pleasant and four million tonnes at 2.4 g/t for 310,000 ounces at Ora Banda. Both projects are in Western Australia.

Gold production for the quarter totalled 46,089 ounces at an average cash operating cost of A$390 per ounce, compared with 42,475 ounces at an average cash operating cost of A$457 per ounce in the March quarter.
Current hedging and commitments totalled 898,250 ounces of gold at an average price of A$530 per ounce, Centaur said.

The company said major contracts continued to be signed for the development of its Cawse nickel/cobalt project in Western Australia with site earthworks having commenced in May 1997 and commissioning expected in July 1998.
The balance of the required project was expected to be finalised in the September 1997 quarter.
The Cawse project has recorded 193 million tonnes at 0.7 percent nickel and 0.04 percent cobalt.
Centaur said additional lateritic nickel and cobalt mineralisation ahd been found at the Siberia joint venture about 25 kilometres north-west of Cawse.
By 12.50 p.m. (0250 GMT), Centaur shares were three cents firmer at A$1.57 on turnover of 661,864 shares.
